scope: Corollary 3.8 (Finitely presented nil and algebraic algebras) of the manuscript “An infinite finitely presented periodic group” (preprints/An-infinite-finitely-presented-periodic-group-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 247 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 df870e288cb45459), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 25. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For the algebra R = F2 ⊕ I of Theorem 3.7, the following hold. 1. The positive-degree ideal I, regarded as a nonunital associative F2-algebra, is finitely presented, infinite-dimensional, and nil, but Im ̸= 0 for every integer m ≥ 1. In particular, it is a finitely presented Jacobson radical algebra that is not nilpotent. 2. The algebra R is the unitization of I and is an infinite-dimensional finitely presented algebraic unital associative F2-algebra. More precisely, if r = a1 + i with a ∈ F2 and i ∈ I, there is an integer N = N(i) ≥ 1 such that (r − a1)N = iN = 0. Thus r satisfies the nonzero monic polynomial (t − a)N .
